You are Agent DEBUG ⟡ — Performance & Bug Hunter for josephibrahim.com (a VFX artist portfolio built with Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript).

Your expertise: React performance patterns, bundle analysis, memory leaks, hydration issues, accessibility. Think like a senior frontend engineer doing a pre-launch audit.

## YOUR 3 TASKS (research only, no code changes):

### Task B1: React Performance Audit
Read all components and evaluate:
- Are there unnecessary re-renders? (state in wrong component, missing memo boundaries)
- Are expensive computations properly memoized? (useMemo, useCallback)
- Are there effects that should be event handlers instead?
- Are scroll listeners properly passive?
- Are refs used appropriately for DOM manipulation vs state?
- Memory leaks? (missing cleanup in useEffect)
- State that should be derived instead of stored?

### Task B2: Bundle & Loading Audit
- Which components use 'use client'? Are any unnecessarily client-side?
- Are heavy dependencies (Vimeo player) lazy-loaded properly?
- Are images using loading="lazy"?
- Could any components be server components instead?
- Are there barrel imports that hurt tree-shaking?

### Task B3: Accessibility & SEO Audit
- Are all interactive elements keyboard-accessible?
- Do images have meaningful alt text?
- Is heading hierarchy correct? (h1 → h2 → h3, no skips)
- Are ARIA attributes correct?
- Is Schema.org structured data complete?
- Are Open Graph meta tags working?

Read ALL these files:
- app/page.tsx
- app/layout.tsx
- app/info/page.tsx
- app/process/page.tsx
- app/process/[slug]/page.tsx
- app/photo/page.tsx
- components/HeroReel.tsx
- components/LadderGrid.tsx
- components/VideoThumbnail.tsx
- components/ChatBot.tsx
- components/Navigation.tsx
- components/ProjectCard.tsx
- components/ProjectDetailContent.tsx
- components/EmbeddedVideoPlayer.tsx
- lib/hooks/useIsMobile.ts
- lib/hooks/usePrefersReducedMotion.ts
- lib/perception/context.tsx
- lib/perception/sensor.ts
- lib/vimeo.ts

Format each finding as:
**[SEVERITY]** file:line — Description of issue → Suggested fix

Severity: CRITICAL (causes bugs/crashes), HIGH (performance impact), MEDIUM (best practice violation), LOW (minor improvement)

Let me compile my comprehensive audit. --- # Performance & Bug Audit Report: josephibrahim.com ## Task B1: React Performance Audit --- **[HIGH]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\page.tsx`:37 -- `scrollProgress` state in `HeroReel.tsx` causes full component re-render on every scroll tick. The `setScrollProgress` call on line 170 of `HeroReel.tsx` triggers a React re-render for every scroll event, even though `scrollProgress` is only used to compute inline styles. This defeats the otherwise excellent pattern of direct DOM manipulation used in `page.tsx`. --> Suggested fix: Convert `scrollProgress` to a ref and apply it via direct DOM manipulation (same pattern as `page.tsx` line 99-141), or use `requestAnimationFrame` throttling around `setScrollProgress`. **[HIGH]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\HeroReel.tsx`:37 -- `scrollProgress` stored as state triggers re-renders on scroll. The `setScrollProgress(progress)` on line 170 fires on every scroll event. Since `scrollOpacity` (line 206) is derived from `scrollProgress` and used only in inline styles, this triggers a full re-render of HeroReel (including the Vimeo iframe wrapper) on every scroll frame. --> Suggested fix: Use a ref + direct DOM style manipulation instead of `useState` for `scrollProgress`. Apply `heroOpacity` directly to the DOM element via a ref. **[HIGH]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\Navigation.tsx`:30 -- `scrollProgress` state causes Navigation to re-render on every scroll. Line 131 calls `setScrollProgress(progress)` in the scroll handler, which triggers a full re-render of the Navigation component (including all child Links) on every scroll event. --> Suggested fix: Use a ref + direct DOM manipulation to update `backgroundColor` opacity. The scroll handler already computes the value -- just apply it to the nav element's style directly. **[HIGH]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\photo\page.tsx`:156 -- Excessive state updates during warm-up animation. The warm-up effect creates ~90 individual `setTimeout` callbacks (one per photo), each calling `setWarmedUpPhotos` which creates a new `Set` and triggers a re-render. That is ~90 re-renders in rapid succession during page load. --> Suggested fix: Batch the warm-up using `requestAnimationFrame` or accumulate indices and update state in fewer batches (e.g., groups of 10-15). Alternatively, use CSS-only animation with staggered `animation-delay` on each photo, avoiding React state entirely. **[HIGH]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\photo\page.tsx`:207-228 -- Glow wave effect creates O(n) state updates per wave. Each wave creates `photosPerWave * 2` (24) timeouts, each calling `setGlowingPhotos` which clones a `Set` and triggers a re-render. Over time this produces continuous re-renders at ~30ms intervals. --> Suggested fix: Use CSS classes toggled via direct DOM manipulation (`element.classList.add/remove`) instead of React state for the glow effect. The glow is purely visual and does not need React's reconciliation. **[MEDIUM]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\LadderGrid.tsx`:31-33 -- Module-level mutable globals for scroll state. `globalHasReachedBottom`, `globalScrollingUpFromBottom`, and `globalLastScrollY` are module-level variables shared across all `ScrollAnimatedCard` instances. While the cleanup on line 191 resets them, during HMR or concurrent rendering these could produce stale or inconsistent values across card instances. --> Suggested fix: Move the global scroll state into a React context or a single shared `useEffect` in `LadderGrid` that passes the computed values down, rather than relying on module-level mutation from multiple effect callbacks. **[MEDIUM]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\LadderGrid.tsx`:68-159 -- Each `ScrollAnimatedCard` registers its own scroll listener. With ~10-15 projects, this means 10-15 separate scroll event listeners, each doing `getBoundingClientRect()`. While each uses `requestAnimationFrame` for debouncing, the RAF callbacks all fire in the same frame, causing 10-15 layout reads per scroll frame. --> Suggested fix: Use a single scroll listener in `LadderGrid` that iterates all card refs, or use `IntersectionObserver` for the initial reveal and only attach scroll listeners for cards currently in view. **[MEDIUM]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\ChatBot.tsx`:233 -- `messages` array in `sendMessage` dependency causes stale closure. The `sendMessage` callback depends on `messages` state, but also calls `setMessages`. The conversation history captured on line 233 (`const conversationHistory = messages.map(...)`) could be stale if `sendMessage` is called rapidly. Additionally, every time `messages` changes, `sendMessage` is recreated, which cascades to `handleSubmit` and `handleQuickReply` recreation. --> Suggested fix: Use a ref to track `messages` for the API call payload, and use the functional form of `setMessages` exclusively. Remove `messages` from the `sendMessage` dependency array. **[MEDIUM]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\components\ChatBot.tsx`:403 -- Using array index as key for messages (`key={index}`). When messages are streamed and the array grows, React's reconciliation with index keys may cause incorrect DOM reuse for the streaming message at the end of the list. --> Suggested fix: Generate a unique ID for each message when created (e.g., `Date.now()` + counter) and use that as the key. **[MEDIUM]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\app\process\page.tsx`:28 -- `ProcessCard` manages hover state with `useState`, causing a full re-render on every mouse enter/leave. Each card re-renders its entire subtree (thumbnail image, title, excerpt, meta row) just to change a few style properties. --> Suggested fix: Use CSS `:hover` pseudo-class for the style changes (opacity, transform, color), or use a ref for direct DOM manipulation. All the hover effects are simple CSS-expressible transitions. **[LOW]** `C:\Users\User\josephibrahim\lib\perception\context.tsx`:44-51 -- Initialization side effects during render.
